messages.author: dc83f318e1e834c9
messages.subject: Retrieve standardized coefficients for semTable
parts:
Hi,
I want to publish the results of my SEM's with lavaan by printing the results in LaTeX. Unfortunately, my code only prints the unstandardized estimates. This is my current code:

sem1 <- sem(a_n_0, 
            data=a,
            estimator     = "WLSMV",
            mimic         = "Mplus",
            start = "Mplus",
            meanstructure = T,
            ordered = c("D_V",
                        "AN_V",
                        "AIMAX",
                        "O_V",  
                        "C_V",
                        "AD_V"))

sem2 <- sem(a_a_0, 
            data=a,
            estimator     = "WLSMV",
            mimic         = "Mplus",
            start = "Mplus",
            meanstructure = T,
            ordered = c("D_V",
                        "AN_V",
                        "AIMAX",
                        "O_V",  
                        "C_V",
                        "AD_V"))

semTable(list("A N"=sem1,"A, N EM"=sem2),
         columns = c(est = "Estimate", se = "SE", p = "p"),
         fits=c("chisq","cfi","rmsea","srmr"),
         paramSets = c("fits","loadings","slopes","latentcovariances","latentvariances","intercepts"),
         caption="DMAP & Emotional Maltreatment",
         centering="siunitx",
         longtable=T,
         type="latex",
         file="sem-table1.tex")

Any suggestions on how to modify my code are highly appreciated.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Retrieve standardized coefficients for semTable
parts: Any suggestions on how to modify my code are highly appreciated.

Have you read the package's vignette?

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/semTable/vignettes/semtable.pdf

A problem of their approach is that you can't trust the SEs (or thus the z or p values) when refitting the model with standardized observed variables.  Not sure why they don't just allow access to those columns of parameterEstimates() with the columns= argument, or even a flag to use standardizedSolution() output instead.  Perhaps write the maintainer.

Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
